What happens to my Steam when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Short answer: Steam games are licences, not property you own. The Steam Subscriber Agreement says your account is strictly personal and that accounts and subscriptions can't be transferred unless Valve specifically permits it. Valve also says it doesn't recognise transfers made outside Steam, including by operation of law. Don't count on passing a Steam library to heirs.

Key facts

  • Games are licences
  • Account is 'strictly personal'
  • No transfer unless Valve permits it
  • Transfers by operation of law aren't recognised

How do I prepare my Steam account?

  1. Treat your Steam library as non-transferable when planning your estate.
  2. Decide what should happen to the account and note it in your wishes.
  3. Keep game saves and any mods or screenshots you care about backed up locally.
  4. Note any Steam Wallet balance or marketplace items in your inventory list.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Valve publishes no deceased-user process. Contact Steam Support for the account.

How long does it take?

No published process or timeframe.

What can't be recovered?

  • The game library itself, in most cases
  • Steam Wallet funds and items tied to the account

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Steam when I die?

Steam games are licences, not property you own. The Steam Subscriber Agreement says your account is strictly personal and that accounts and subscriptions can't be transferred unless Valve specifically permits it. Valve also says it doesn't recognise transfers made outside Steam, including by operation of law. Don't count on passing a Steam library to heirs.

Can I leave my Steam games in my will?

Valve's Subscriber Agreement says accounts and subscriptions can't be transferred unless Valve specifically permits it, so a will alone doesn't move them.

Can my kids keep playing on my account?

The agreement says you may not share your password or account except as Valve authorises.

Is this different from physical games?

Yes. Discs and cartridges are property; Steam purchases are licences.
